page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Running on the KVM hypervisor, it is configured with 64 dedicated Ampere Altra vCPUs clocked at 2.8 GHz and 256.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core). The instance includes no integrated GPU hardware and provides no local storage, relying on external network volumes alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-threaded execution and memory cache throughput. The instance achieved 114463.22 on the stress-ng multi-core benchmark and 413.03 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, both falling into the top quartile of tested machines. Small-block cached read memory bandwidth reached 4547.11 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput key-value processing as reflected by 82.33 million operations per second in Redis SET testing. Conversely, single-core metrics are moderate, with single-core stress-ng scoring 1790.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression recording 8.01 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration provides high physical core density and predictable CPU scheduling without hyperthreading contention. Tradeoffs include lower single-threaded processing speeds compared to high-clock x86 architectures and the lack of bundled local NVMe storage. The instance is structured for multi-threaded, parallelized cloud workloads such as in-memory caching tiers, container orchestration nodes, backend web services, and distributed microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.16xlarge is a general-purpose server based on the arm64 architecture, powered by Ampere Altra processors running at 2.8 GHz. It is provisioned with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM, offering a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Operating on KVM, the instance features a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero local disk storage, and no GPU accelerators. Performance metrics show top-tier multi-core compute and cache throughput, marked by strong results in stress-ng multi-core tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Redis SET throughput reaching 82.33 million operations per second. Single-core performance and uncached memory bandwidth remain in average tiers. The platform provides consistent parallel compute density, suiting container clusters, Redis caching nodes, and multi-threaded enterprise application backends.
